new_bars.name: Cantina OK!
new_bars.bio: A standing-room-only mezcal bar for about 20 people, set in a converted garage down Council Place, a short laneway off Clarence Street. Opened in 2019 by Jeremy Blackmore and Alex Dowd of Tio's Cerveceria (now MUCHO Group), it pours hand-sourced agave spirits and margaritas over hand-cranked shaved ice. No. 96 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2024.
new_bars.why: Sydney's tiny agave landmark: World's 50 Best Bars No. 96 (2024) and Australian Tequila Bar of the Year 2025 and 2026.

new_bars.name: Bar Planet
new_bars.bio: A playful, space-age martini bar at the Newtown end of Enmore Road, opened in 2022 by the MUCHO Group team behind Cantina OK! (Jeremy Blackmore, Alex Dowd and Daisy Tulley). The house martini is built on a seasonal in-house spirit and poured from height out of a porrón, alongside a short list of fresh, fruit-led cocktails. Australian Gin Bar of the Year in 2025 and 2026.
new_bars.why: The Inner West's martini temple, back-to-back Gin Bar of the Year at the Australian Bar Awards.

new_bars.name: Old Mate's Place
new_bars.bio: A two-level bar on the top floor of 199 Clarence Street, with a whisky- and rum-heavy back bar downstairs and a hidden rooftop above. Opened in August 2018 by Andres and Gabrielle Walters and Daniel Noble, it is loved by the trade for fun, fruit-forward drinks and easygoing service. Australian Bar of the Year 2025 and Best Bartenders' Bar 2026.
new_bars.why: Named Australia's Bar of the Year in 2025 and the country's Best Bartenders' Bar in 2026.

new_bars.name: Old Love's
new_bars.bio: A tiki-leaning rum bar in the basement of 199 Clarence Street, opened in late 2023 by the Old Mate's Place team led by Dre Walters. Guests get a house 'Book of Rum', the back bar is shelved in the same order as the book, and the drinks revive old Caribbean and Pacific recipes. Rum Bar of the Year 2024, 2025 and 2026; its Callum Marra was 2026 Australian Bartender of the Year.
new_bars.why: Three straight Rum Bar of the Year wins (2024-2026) and home of the 2026 Australian Bartender of the Year.

new_bars.name: Dean & Nancy on 22
new_bars.bio: A mid-century style hotel bar on level 22 of A by Adina Sydney, opened in 2021 and run with the Maybe Sammy team. Black and gold interiors, a brass staircase, a grand piano and skyline views frame the 'Time Machine' list of cocktails inspired by 1950s and 60s legends and pop culture. Australian Hotel Bar of the Year in 2024 and 2025.
new_bars.coord_source: osm way 409035079 (A by Adina tower at George and Hunter Streets, tagged 'Adina Grand')
new_bars.why: Sydney's standout hotel bar, Hotel Bar of the Year at the Australian Bar Awards in 2024 and 2025.

new_bars.name: Bar Tilda
new_bars.bio: A moody, marble-clad hotel bar off Phillip Street in the Sofitel Sydney Wentworth, opened in October 2024 by House Made Hospitality with drinks by Jason Williams and Christian Blair. Its showpieces are an armoire holding more than 100 Australian whiskies and an Archie Rose martini trolley mixed at the table, plus live music. Australian Hotel Bar of the Year 2026.
new_bars.why: A new-wave hotel bar built around Australian whisky and tableside martinis; Hotel Bar of the Year 2026.

new_bars.name: Ramblin' Rascal Tavern
new_bars.bio: A self-styled five-star dive bar in a basement near the corner of Park and Elizabeth Streets, marked only by a sign with three skulls. Opened in 2014 by former Swillhouse bartenders Charlie Lehmann, Dardan Shervashidze and Sebastian Soto, it pairs a deep cognac and whisky back bar with cheap tins, sharp cocktails and live music four nights a week. Best Bartenders' Bar 2025.
new_bars.why: The industry's favourite after-shift dive, named Best Bartenders' Bar at the 2025 Australian Bar Awards.

new_bars.name: The Baxter Inn
new_bars.bio: The basement whisky bar that helped define Sydney's small-bar era, hidden at the end of an alley off Clarence Street. Opened in 2011 by Swillhouse founders Anton Forte and Jason Scott, it is known for a towering wall of whisky, staff happy to talk through any bottle, pretzels and a short list of seasonal house cocktails. Walk-in only, open until 3am.
new_bars.why: Historic pick: the 2011 whisky den that set the template for Sydney's hidden laneway bars and is still packed nightly.

new_bars.name: PS40
new_bars.bio: A cocktail bar and soda lab off Skittle Lane in the CBD, opened in 2016 by Michael Chiem and Thor Bergquist and owned solely by Chiem since 2019. House sodas such as wattle cola and bush tonic are made and poured on tap, and the list applies kitchen techniques to native Australian flavours. Its signature Africola remains one of the city's best-known drinks.
new_bars.why: Ten years on, still Sydney's most inventive small bar, built around its own native-flavoured soda program.

new_bars.name: Deadwax
new_bars.bio: A Japanese-inspired vinyl listening bar on Enmore Road, opened in August 2025 by Conor O'Brien and Dan Teh of Otis. Hi-fi sound, a large record library, DJs at weekends and a bar top made from 70 layers of resin-soaked denim set the scene for Japanese-leaning riffs on classics, a big Japanese whisky range and late-night snacks. A 2026 finalist for Australia's New Bar of the Year.
new_bars.coord_source: geocoded street number: interpolated between osm-addressed 164 and 192 Enmore Road (no venue or number 182 in OSM)
new_bars.why: The most talked-about new opening of 2025 on Sydney's liveliest bar strip, pairing listening-bar culture with Japanese technique.

new_bars.name: Apollonia
new_bars.bio: A basement bar beneath Hinchcliff House near Circular Quay, imagined as a Sicilian bandit's drinking den and named for Apollonia from The Godfather. Opened in April 2021 by House Made Hospitality, with drinks overseen by former Australian Bartender of the Year Jason Williams, it is known for Negronis and an Italian-leaning 'Playbill' menu told in four acts.
new_bars.why: A distinctive Italian-themed late-night bar, 2026 finalist for both Bar of the Year and Cocktail List of the Year.

drinks.name: Spoonful

drinks.name: Silk Sonic

drinks.name: Mum's Breakfast
drinks.description: Gin with mandarin-infused dry vermouth, mandarin jam, lemon and egg white.

drinks.name: Tombstone
drinks.description: Co-owner Charlie Lehmann's early signature: Booker's bourbon, sugar and barrel-aged bitters, shaken hard and served up with a cherry.

drinks.name: Crimson Peel

drinks.name: Old Money
drinks.description: Tanqueray gin with late harvest semillon, quinine and Peychaud's bitters, served up.

drinks.name: Tap Old Fashioned
drinks.description: The bar's on-tap old fashioned: bourbon, bitters and sugar poured over ice.

drinks.name: Africola

notes: Maybe Sammy (existing handle maybe_sammy_sydney): 2025 top-50 position (No. 42) intentionally omitted; added 2024 No. 26 (source: Time Out Sydney report of the results, as the50.com 2024 1-50 page now shows 2025) and 2026 No. 75 on the 51-100 list published 23 Sep 2026. The 2026 top 50 is announced 7 Oct 2026, after this research.
No Sydney bar won a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award in 2024, 2025 or 2026 (checked the official winners pages). Asia's and North America's 50 Best do not cover Australia.

Australian Bar Awards results are from australianbartender.com.au (Bartender Magazine's site). Person awards were not entered as bar awards: Callum Marra of Old Love's was 2026 Bartender of the Year; Alicia Clarke (Double Deuce) was 2025 Bar Manager of the Year; House Made Hospitality (Apollonia, Bar Tilda) was 2025 Bar Operator of the Year.

Cantina OK!'s own news post says it won Tequila Bar of the Year three years running, but the 2024 official winners list shows Centro 86 for that category, so only 2025 and 2026 are entered. cantinaok.com.au did not resolve, so website is the MUCHO Group venue page (which is also the OSM website tag).
Double Deuce Lounge (NSW Cocktail Bar of the Year 2024 state award) has closed; MUCHO's Bar Bridge opened in its Bridge Street site in 2026. Not included.

Old Mate's Place and Old Love's share a building and owners (Old Mates Group); Cantina OK! and Bar Planet share MUCHO Group; Dean & Nancy on 22 is run with the Maybe Sammy team; Bar Tilda and Apollonia are both House Made Hospitality. Kept because each has a distinct concept and its own awards.

The Baxter Inn is included for historic importance (no 2024-2026 list awards found). Its owner, Swillhouse, was the subject of 2024 press reports alleging workplace misconduct; reviewer may want to weigh that.
Ramblin' Rascal Tavern: its website gives 199 Elizabeth Street; OSM tags the node as 197 Elizabeth Street and older press uses the building's 60 Park Street address. Website address used.

Deadwax: no OSM node for the venue or for number 182, so coordinates are interpolated along the even-numbered side of Enmore Road between 164 and 192; treat as approximate (within ~30 m). Old Love's and PS40 drinks come from 2023-era sources (Concrete Playground review; PS40's menu page dated a Friday 7 July, likely 2023), so on_current_menu is false. Bar Tilda drinks are from its October 2024 launch coverage, also marked not current.

Dean & Nancy on 22: the OSM building way for the A by Adina tower is tagged 'Adina Grand, 280 George Street'; it matches the 26-storey tower at George and Hunter Streets, and the bar gives its address as Level 22, 2 Hunter Street.
